content.value_statement: Federal FFP estimates require traceable wages, indirect costs, benchmarks, travel, and formulas. This skill builds a validated workbook with visible assumptions and sourced calculations.
actual_capabilities: Decomposes approved requirements into labor categories, SOC mappings, staffing, periods, and deliverables.
Retrieves current BLS wage percentiles and applies a formula-driven aging adjustment.
Builds layered fringe, overhead, G&A, profit, and fully burdened rate calculations.
Positions proposed rates against CALC+ percentiles without making acquisition determinations.
Calculates supported travel costs and preserves explicit exclusions or zero-cost rows.
Validates workbook structure, independent calculations, and optional LibreOffice formula execution.
limitations: Supports firm-fixed-price estimates only, not labor-hour, T&M, cost-reimbursement, or grant budgets.
Requires configured BLS OEWS, GSA CALC, and relevant GSA Per Diem MCP capabilities.
Does not originate fair-and-reasonable conclusions, negotiation positions, or Contracting Officer judgments.
Cannot claim independent formula execution when Excel or LibreOffice is unavailable.

use_cases.title: Build an acquisition IGCE
use_cases.description: Create a seven-sheet FFP workbook from approved staffing, location, period, vehicle, and travel assumptions.

use_cases.title: Test cost assumptions
use_cases.description: Compare vehicle presets, approved indirect rates, and low, mid, and high scenarios with visible component arithmetic.

use_cases.title: Position proposed rates
use_cases.description: Compare proposed FFP rates with BLS and CALC+ percentiles while leaving the acquisition determination to authorized officials.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic FFP estimate
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an FFP IGCE for [labor categories] in [location] for [period]. Use [FTE] staffing and identify any missing required inputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has structured labor and performance inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Build from a requirement
prompt_templates.prompt: Decompose this SOW or PWS into candidate labor categories and SOC codes. Present Stage A for my confirmation before asking pricing questions: [requirement].
prompt_templates.scenario: A user needs staffing decomposition before cost modeling.

prompt_templates.title: Compare pricing scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: Build low, mid, and high FFP scenarios using [vehicle or approved rates]. Show each burden component, implied multiplier, escalation, travel, and period totals.
prompt_templates.scenario: An analyst needs transparent sensitivity testing.

prompt_templates.title: Validate proposed FFP rates
prompt_templates.prompt: Position these proposed rates against current BLS wages and CALC+ percentiles: [rates]. Keep title-match and experience-match pools separate and provide no determination.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced reviewer needs neutral benchmark evidence.

output_examples.input: Build a three-year FFP IGCE for four software roles in Washington, DC, with no travel.
output_examples.output: A seven-sheet workbook shows sourced wages, aging, burden layers, annual options, scenarios, benchmark positioning, explicit zero travel, and validation results.

output_examples.input: Compare proposed senior engineer rates with CALC+ and BLS data.
output: A neutral table lists proposed rates beside CALC+ P25, P50, P75, and P90 values.
A separate section shows BLS metro wages and burdened equivalents.
Notes identify sample size, matching method, fallback sources, and positioning bands without a verdict.

output_examples.input: Price an 18-month study by four weighted deliverables.
output_examples.output: The workbook allocates labor and travel by approved weights, checks that weights total 100%, and prices milestones using documented timing assumptions.

best_practices: Provide approved staffing, location, contract start, period structure, vehicle basis, and travel assumptions before the build.
Review every ambiguous SOC mapping, fallback source, indirect-rate basis, and deliverable allocation.
Run all available validation layers and disclose whether a real spreadsheet engine executed formulas.
anti_patterns: Do not use this workflow for labor-hour, T&M, cost-reimbursement, or grant estimates.
Do not treat benchmark positioning as a fair-and-reasonable determination.
Do not hardcode aging factors, hourly row references, or unsupported premiums inside formulas.

faq.question: What inputs are required?
faq.answer: Provide labor categories or task areas, location, staffing basis, productive hours, performance period, contract start, pricing structure, and vehicle basis.

faq.question: Which data sources does the skill use?
faq.answer: It uses BLS OEWS wages, GSA CALC+ ceiling-rate data, and GSA Per Diem data when travel applies.

faq.question: Can it decide whether a price is fair and reasonable?
faq.answer: No. It provides sourced arithmetic and neutral positioning data while reserving the determination for the Contracting Officer.

faq.question: Can it build from a SOW or PWS?
faq.answer: Yes. It first presents a staged labor and SOC decomposition for user confirmation, then collects pricing inputs.

faq.question: How does workbook validation work?
faq.answer: It checks formula structure, recomputes expected values independently, and uses LibreOffice for formula execution when available.

faq.question: What happens when an MCP service is unavailable?
faq.answer: The workflow stops, identifies the missing capability, and reports whether installation or authentication appears to be required.
